deviations: LIML implemented by hand (k-class with kappa = smallest eigenvalue); household-FE LIML run on within-demeaned data. Standard errors for the IV columns are not computed (only coefficients are claimed).

Specification is a reconstruction: price = lnPRE (log kWh price deflated by the CPI index IP in the analysis file); instruments = filled deflated effective prices lnPRE_papas_, lnPRE_aguav_, lnPRE_gascar_ (the unfilled versions have missing values and would cut N below the reported 20,872); income = lny and lny^2; controls = household size, rooms, surface, elderly dummy, renting, building >25 years, urban, province capital, education (4 levels), economic situation (3 levels), municipality size (5), region (CCAA), quarter and year dummies, months since reform (dist); treated-group dummy D (Tm) included in the non-FE models (added after the claim comparison in attempt-3).
notes: Data: analysis CSV 'Data_to run_DOFILE3.csv' (selected columns only). Sample = rows with T2 (post-reform treatment dummy) non-missing (25,775 obs, matching the paper's panel), then complete cases on the regression variables, which gives exactly 20,872 obs and 10,729 households (the economic-situation variable SITUACTHOG_j drives the drop). attempt-1 and attempt-2 were exploratory (variable inspection, sample counts). attempt-3 was the first estimating run; after comparing it with the claims I added the treated-group dummy D (Tm) and stopped there. N, households and both price elasticities match. The OLS reform effects come out smaller in absolute value than reported (-0.134 vs -0.178; -0.139 vs -0.156). The FE consumption effect is close (-0.166 vs -0.154). The FE expenditure effects (-0.151 and -0.160 vs -0.098 and -0.089) and the FE-IV effects differ. The paper's expenditure and consumption reform effects differ more than the accounting identity ln g = ln p + ln q allows with my variables, which suggests a differently defined (for example deflated) expenditure or price variable that I could not identify. No authors' scripts were opened.
